content: To prove barycentric subdivision, Andrew and I need a topology on finite dimensional (geometric) simplices. Andrew originally used docs#stdSimplex which, by virtue of being a set, inherits the subtype topology of the corresponding pi type, ie the one coming from the L^infty norm.

However, stdSimplex is "old convexity flavored", and my medium term goal is to replace it with docs#Convexity.StdSimplex. StdSimplex R X naturally embeds into X →₀ R, and therefore it is natural to pull the topology from docs#Finsupp back onto StdSimplex.
But now! Finsupp currently doesn't have any topology, so what should that topology be?

In #40212, I suggest (in the case where the codomain is a metric space) the L^1 metric, on the basis that its dual is the L^infty metric on the pi type, which is indeed the default metric for pi types.
My answer would be : none by default. The issue is that docs#Finsupp is an inductive limit, and inductive limits in different topological categories typically yield different topologies

For example, when you take the direct sum of TVSs, you want to take the inductive limit in the category of TVSs. But then if they are locally convex you may want to take the limit in the category of LCTVSs
Would you then be happy with the L^p metric on WithLp p (ι →₀ X)?
Well actually in this case I think they coincide
But in any case I would be very careful before putting any topology on this kind of objects
Anatole, does your argument extend to not having a topology by default on StdSimplex?
I don’t know. I will think about it.

Yaël Dillies said:

Would you then be happy with the L^p metric on WithLp p (ι →₀ X)?

Sure.
